The opportunity

The lowest-priced entry to the most heavily funded block in Blacksburg.

Directly across Grove Avenue from this front yard, the old high school site is cleared and about to break ground: up to 73 townhomes priced from the $600s, with roughly 20 acres staying public as parks, trails, and ballfields. I represent the developer building it, so I know exactly what is coming and when. Zillow puts the typical 24060 home at $434,185. Homes here sell at 99.2 percent of asking, in a market with about 3.6 months of supply. My job is to make sure the Foundation captures every dollar that investment adds to this address, and my plan below shows two clean paths to do it: list as-is at $335,000 and let investor demand compete, or invest $52,500 with my contractor team and list at $450,000 or above.

Either way, I will not market this listing to Blacksburg alone. I will put it in front of Hokie Nation: 299,415 living alumni, including more than 60,000 in greater Washington and active chapters in Tidewater and the Peninsula, through my network in Northern Virginia, Virginia Beach, and the Lunch Pail Ventures community.

01 · The property

Brick, hardwood, and a yard the new construction can't match

Solid 1955 bones in Blacksburg Heights. Original oak floors run under most of the main level, the layout is the classic three-bedroom ranch buyers ask for, and the primary bedroom has its own full bath, a rarity at this vintage.

Address803 Grove Ave, Blacksburg, VA 24060

Heat / coolHeat pump with central air
ExtrasFireplace, rear deck, 10x10 shed (2003), mature shade trees
2026 assessment$247,600 ($60,000 land / $187,600 improvements)

The house presents exactly the way a value-add buyer hopes: cosmetically tired, structurally honest. The kitchen and both baths are original-era and price into any offer. What does not need buying: brick exterior, gable roof, hardwood, the mechanical basics, and a genuinely large back yard shaded by mature trees.

What the county card misses The Montgomery County record shows one full bath. There are two: the second is a shower bath off the primary suite, effectively a primary suite the assessment does not know exists. Neither does the size of the back yard. Buyers relying on public records will underestimate this house, which is precisely why the marketing has to lead with photography and a corrected fact sheet, and why the assessment is a floor, not a signal of value.

Across the road, right now

The old high school site is about to break ground

The former Blacksburg High School is gone and the site is cleared, with grading ahead of construction next. Approved for the parcel: up to 73 townhomes expected to start around $600,000 to $650,000, while roughly 20.6 acres stay public, with parks, connected walking and biking trails, and the existing track, ballfields, and pickleball courts remaining. The town is even studying this site for a major new recreation facility.

I represent the developer of this project. The Foundation gets a broker with first-hand knowledge of what is being built across the street and on what timeline, and the house across the street from $600K new construction is the cheapest way to own the block.

05 · The renovation option

If you renovate: $52,500 in, about $62,500 more out, and I manage all of it.

Most sellers in the Foundation's position choose as-is, and this plan is built for that. But the decision deserves the full picture: four well-chosen projects, priced from my experience with renovations small and large in this market, coordinated by me with contractors I have vetted on my own projects.

Kitchen, full refresh$20,000

New cabinets, counters, appliances, lighting. The single highest-leverage dollar in the house.

Both baths$15,000

Hall tub bath and the primary suite's shower bath, fixtures to finishes.

Flooring$10,000

Refinish the oak that is already there, new flooring where it is not.

Paint, whole interior$7,500

Every wall, ceiling, and trim line, one cohesive palette.

Total scope$52,500

Figures are planning estimates from my own renovation projects in this market, firmed up with contractor bids before any commitment. The Foundation approves every line.

The differentiator

The buyer for this house probably does not live in Blacksburg yet

Southern Living just profiled the trend: alumni buying second homes back in their college towns, and Blacksburg by name. The 24060 market already prices that demand. My plan puts 803 Grove in front of it deliberately, as a game day home, a future retirement landing spot, or a house for a student with parents who would rather build equity than pay rent.
